dek: Sandstone Falls at New River Gorge is a 390-foot boardwalk walk, not a hike. There's no entrance fee, and the falls run year-round and strongest in spring.
overview: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve covers more than 70,000 acres along a rugged river that flows north. The park describes the New River as one of the oldest on the continent.

Sandstone Falls is the waterfall we cover here, and visitors have reviewed it heavily. Our trail file lists the Sandstone Falls Boardwalk at 390 feet one way. The park's notes say the falls run year-round and are strong in spring, and that there is no activity fee at the site.
fallsIntro: Sandstone Falls is a boardwalk walk of 390 feet one way, so its distance is in feet rather than miles.
plan: The visit is the boardwalk: 390 feet from the parking lot, a short walk. Spring is the season with strong flow, and the park's notes say the falls don't dry up in summer.
flow: The nearest gauge with a complete record is the Greenbrier River at Hilldale (USGS 03184000), about 10 miles from Sandstone Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in February at about 5,420 cubic feet per second and was lowest in October at about 453.
That gauge is on a different river from the falls, so use it as a regional picture. The park's own note that Sandstone Falls is strongest in spring is the better guide.
feesLead: There is no entrance fee, and the park's notes say there is no activity fee at Sandstone Falls either.
access: The park's own pages cover access to the boardwalk, and we don't have a shuttle or timed-entry rule on file. Hinton is the nearest town in our index, about 6 miles away in a straight line.
safety: We have no hazard warnings on file specific to the boardwalk. The park describes the river as whitewater in a deep canyon, so keep to the boardwalk and stay out of the river.
